answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie identity and reputation to costly, slowly accumulated stake that cannot be cheaply cloned. Think of trust like a glacier moving through a canyon: it takes time and pressure to form, and a new fake agent cannot instantly carve the same path. Reputation scores stay crystal clear only when they are earned through verifiable work and bonded collateral, so spawning thousands of sockpuppet agents yields no shortcut around that cost.
